Learned <Term id="world-model">world models</Term> and physics simulators both predict what an action does: MuJoCo computes it from explicit geometry, dynamics and contact rules <Cite id="mujoco-2012" />, while a learned model predicts it from data. Physics suits mechanics that can be specified and actions no dataset covers, learning suits appearance and contact that are costly to model, and many systems combine the two.

## They solve different specification problems

MuJoCo models articulated bodies, constraints and contact with explicit equations and parameters <Cite id="mujoco-2012" />. Isaac Lab wraps GPU simulation, sensors, task definitions and batched environments into a robot-learning workflow <Cite id="isaac-lab-2025" />. Disney Research, Google DeepMind and NVIDIA gave their Newton GPU engine to the Linux Foundation in September 2025 <Cite id="newton-lf-2025" />. NVIDIA reports that MuJoCo Warp speeds up MJX by 252x on locomotion and 475x on manipulation on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU <Cite id="newton-manipulation-blog-2026" />.

A learned world model estimates transitions from observations and actions, often in a latent or video space, and trades parameter error for dataset and generalization error. Hansen and Wang call hallucination "inherently a data coverage issue" <Cite id="wm-hallucination-2026" />. A 2026 survey lists simulation among a world model's roles, with planning, policy learning, evaluation and data generation <Cite id="world-model-survey-2026" />.

Model-based robot learning is the family of methods that learn how the world responds to actions and use that model to plan, to train a policy in imagination, or both. Its two steps are learning a dynamics model and integrating planning with learning <Cite id="mbrl-survey-2020" />.

<Image id="daydreamer-a1-rollover-2022" />

The loop predicts futures under candidate actions, scores them, acts, observes the real transition and updates the model. Sutton proposed integrated architectures for learning, planning and reacting in 1990 <Cite id="dyna-1990" />.

<ModelBasedLoop className="my-6" />

<SelfCheck
  prompt="A learned dynamics model produces sharp videos but predicts nearly the same future for three different gripper actions. What is the diagnosis?"
  options={[
    {
      value: 'useful-model',
      label: 'The model is useful for planning because its videos look photorealistic',
      why: 'Visual fidelity cannot select among actions when the rollout ignores the candidate action. The model may be a good generator and a poor control model.'
    },
    {
      value: 'action-collapse',
      label: 'The model has action-conditioning collapse and cannot support planning',
      why: 'Planning requires counterfactual separation: different actions must produce meaningfully different predicted consequences. Without it, every candidate receives nearly the same evidence.'
    },
    {
      value: 'longer-rollout',
      label: 'The planner needs a longer prediction horizon',
      why: 'A longer rollout compounds the same missing action dependence. Horizon cannot recover information the one-step transition failed to encode.'
    }
  ]}
  answer="action-collapse"
  takeaway="A control model earns its name by changing its prediction when the candidate action changes."
/>

<span id="the-model-based-decomposition" />
## Model-based means predicting the effect of an action

A 2026 survey defines a world model as "an action-conditioned predictive system" <Cite id="manip-wm-survey-2026" />. Classical model-predictive control (MPC) uses explicit dynamics, such as MuJoCo's rigid-body and contact model <Cite id="mujoco-2012" />; model-based learning fits some or all of that transition to data.

A <Term id="world-model">world model</Term> need not predict pixels: value-equivalent models predict only what planning needs, "without compromising performance" <Cite id="value-equivalence-2020" />. PILCO carries Gaussian-process transition uncertainty into planning and controller learning <Cite id="pilco-2015" />.

<span id="two-ways-to-use-imagined-experience" />
## A model can plan each step or train a policy in imagination

A planner rolls sampled action sequences through the model, executes the best first action and replans, so a new goal or cost needs no retraining, at the price of many rollouts per real step ([reward design and MPC](/rl-sim2real/reward-design-mpc/)). In 2016 Finn and Levine combined action-conditioned video prediction with MPC so a real robot could push novel objects <Cite id="deep-visual-foresight-2016" />. TD-MPC2 trained one 317M-parameter agent on 80 tasks <Cite id="tdmpc2-2023" />, and PointWorld, trained on about 2 million trajectories, plans with MPC at 0.1 s per inference on a real Franka without demonstrations <Cite id="pointworld-2026" />.

Dreamer instead trains a policy on trajectories imagined in a learned latent space <Cite id="dreamer-2019" />, and DreamerV3 covers more than 150 tasks with one configuration <Cite id="dreamerv3-2023" />. Dreamer 4 learns purely offline, a setting its authors tie to robotics, where interaction "can be unsafe and slow" <Cite id="dreamer4-2025" />. [Latent dynamics](/world-models/latent-dynamics/) covers these agents.

<span id="uncertainty-aware-models" />
## Uncertainty estimates keep policies from exploiting model errors

A policy trained on a model "tends to exploit regions where insufficient data is available", which ME-TRPO counters with an ensemble <Cite id="me-trpo-2018" />. PETS, a probabilistic ensemble, matches model-free asymptotic performance with 8 and 125 times fewer samples than SAC and PPO on half-cheetah <Cite id="pets-2018" />. MBPO keeps rollouts short and "branched from real data" <Cite id="mbpo-2019" />. In [offline RL](/rl-sim2real/offline-rl/), MOPO penalizes reward by model uncertainty <Cite id="mopo-2020" />. MOReL learns a pessimistic decision process from offline data and trains its policy within that process <Cite id="morel-2020" />.

<span id="why-physical-robots-make-the-model-harder" />
## Robots see only part of the state, yet learn useful models in minutes to hours

A robot observation is partial: cameras miss forces, friction and compliance, and RGBD gave an 80% improvement in fabric-folding success over RGB <Cite id="visuospatial-foresight-2020" />. Data is narrow too: Hansen and Wang call world-model hallucination "inherently a data coverage issue" and adapt a model to unseen simulated environments with 50 trajectories <Cite id="wm-hallucination-2026" />.

Chenyuan Zhou, Yining Hong, Jiajun Wu and colleagues at Stanford and elsewhere (October 2026) condition a video world model on a 32-dimensional latent for hidden factors such as friction or mass, fitted at test time from one or two interactions while the model stays frozen <Cite id="t2z-2026" />. Averaged over four real-robot tasks, the adapted model's mean tracking error fell from 19.30 to 10.85 pixels against the same model without a latent <Cite id="t2z-2026" />. Actions it picked succeeded 70.80% of the time against 26.47% for the model without a latent, though the paper does not state trial counts <Cite id="t2z-2026" />.

PDDM learned contact-rich manipulation on a 24-DoF hand from 4 real hours <Cite id="pddm-2019" />. DayDreamer ran Dreamer online on 4 robots without simulators; a quadruped learned to stand up and walk in 1 hour <Cite id="daydreamer-2022" />. SSRL adds a learned force ensemble to known Lagrangian dynamics and learned Go1 gaits from a few minutes of data <Cite id="ssrl-2024" />.

In September 2026, Claudio Canales, Marco Hutter and colleagues learned a probabilistic dynamics ensemble from scratch on an 11.5-ton hydraulic excavator. After 20 minutes, their sampling-based MPC tracked comparably to learned controllers trained on 100 to 150 minutes; after 40 it held sub-centimeter mean path error at high speed <Cite id="excavator-mbrl-2026" />. Hansen, Fox and colleagues trained one TD-MPC2 model in simulation on up to 90 insertion tasks, with 56% zero-shot success on unseen objects against 7% model-free <Cite id="insertion-world-models-2026" />.

<ExcavatorPractice className="my-6" />

## Model error is task-weighted

A two-millimeter error is irrelevant in free space and decisive at a tight connector. One-step prediction likelihood "is not always correlated with control performance", and task-effective models "do not necessarily need to be globally accurate" <Cite id="objective-mismatch-2020" />. The 2026 robot world-model survey stresses action-conditioned consistency and functional-utility evaluation <Cite id="world-model-survey-2026" />; the [evaluation guide](/world-models/evaluation/) gives a protocol.

<span id="neural-simulators-and-hybrid-models" />
## Neural and hybrid simulators now train real-robot policies

Robotic World Model trains a neural-network simulator for policy optimization <Cite id="robotic-world-model-2025" />, and RWM-U adds epistemic uncertainty to train real quadruped and humanoid policies entirely offline <Cite id="rwm-u-2025" />. <Image id="roboworld-synthetic-scenes-2026" />

Hybrids keep known physics and learn what it misses: TossingBot learns residuals on a physics-based throw and reached 500+ mean picks per hour <Cite id="tossingbot-2019" />, and ASAP fits a delta action model to real Unitree G1 data <Cite id="asap-2025" />. [World models versus physics simulators](/world-models/world-models-vs-simulators/) compares the options.

<span id="when-to-choose-model-based-learning" />

Model-based robot learning is the family of methods that learn how the world responds to actions and use that model to plan, to train a policy in imagination, or both. Its two steps are learning a dynamics model and integrating planning with learning <Cite id="mbrl-survey-2020" />.

<Image id="daydreamer-a1-rollover-2022" />

The loop predicts futures under candidate actions, scores them, acts, observes the real transition and updates the model. Sutton proposed integrated architectures for learning, planning and reacting in 1990 <Cite id="dyna-1990" />.

  options={[
    {
      value: 'useful-model',
      label: 'The model is useful for planning because its videos look photorealistic',
      why: 'Visual fidelity cannot select among actions when the rollout ignores the candidate action. The model may be a good generator and a poor control model.'

      value: 'action-collapse',
      label: 'The model has action-conditioning collapse and cannot support planning',
      why: 'Planning requires counterfactual separation: different actions must produce meaningfully different predicted consequences. Without it, every candidate receives nearly the same evidence.'

<span id="the-model-based-decomposition" />

A 2026 survey defines a world model as "an action-conditioned predictive system" <Cite id="manip-wm-survey-2026" />. A planner rolls sampled action sequences through the model, executes the best first action and replans, so a new goal or cost needs no retraining, at the price of many rollouts per real step ([reward design and MPC](/rl-sim2real/reward-design-mpc/)). Dreamer instead trains a policy on trajectories imagined in a learned latent space <Cite id="dreamer-2019" />, and DreamerV3 covers more than 150 tasks with one configuration <Cite id="dreamerv3-2023" />. Image metrics cannot establish that: on Physics-IQ, physical understanding in video generators was "unrelated to visual realism" <Cite id="physics-iq-2025" />.

<Image id="simpler-real-vs-sim-2024" />

A 2026 survey of robot world models rates controllability above visual plausibility <Cite id="world-model-survey-2026" />, and the closed-loop World-in-World benchmark found it mattered more than visual quality for task success <Cite id="world-in-world-2025" />.

<WorldModelEvaluationLadder className="my-6" />

<SelfCheck
  prompt="You want to use a video world model to select between two robot policies before hardware testing. Which validation result matters most?"
  options={[
    {
      value: 'policy-ranking',
      label: 'Its policy ranking agrees with repeated real-world policy trials',
      why: 'This directly validates the intended use. The neural evaluator may still be imperfect, but its ordering is calibrated against the decision it will support.'
    },
    {
      value: 'sharpness',
      label: 'Its generated frames receive the highest perceptual sharpness score',
      why: 'Sharpness may improve human inspection, but it does not show that the model preserves action consequences or ranks policies the way the real robot does.'
    },

/>

<span id="start-with-the-intended-use" />
## Perception scores miss function, so each use needs its own test

WorldArena scores 14 models separately as data engines, policy evaluators and action planners, and reports a "significant perception-functionality gap" <Cite id="worldarena-2026" />. NVIDIA reports its DreamGen Bench video scores tracking downstream policy success <Cite id="dreamgen-2025" />. 1X saw unchanged policy weights degrade within days after subtle lighting or background changes <Cite id="1x-world-model-2024" />.

<span id="level-1-one-step-action-sensitivity" />
## Level 1: open models often fail to follow a changed action

Build matched counterfactuals: fix the observation, noise, prompt and history, and change one action dimension. WorldEval found raw action inputs often yield videos that ignore the action <Cite id="worldeval-2025" />, and IRASim and Ctrl-World add frame-level action conditioning <Cite id="irasim-2024" /> <Cite id="ctrl-world-2025" />. Across six open action-conditioned world models and more than 18,000 test instances, WorldSimProbe found systematic degradation in how actions are realized <Cite id="worldsimprobe-2026" />.

<span id="level-2-temporal-and-physical-consistency" />
## Level 2: pooled video metrics hide physical errors

Roll out autoregressively, score task events such as grasp, slip and release, and report error per horizon. Fréchet Video Distance "increases only slightly with large temporal corruption" <Cite id="fvd-content-bias-2024" />. WorldModelBench uses 67K human labels to catch violations such as objects changing size <Cite id="worldmodelbench-2025" />, and video models trained on simple physics failed out of distribution, copying the closest training example <Cite id="video-physical-law-2024" />.

<Image id="roboworld-bair-forcing-2026" />

<span id="level-3-task-progress-scoring" />
## Level 3: the progress scorer needs its own test

Many evaluators pair a video generator with a vision-language scorer, as WorldGym does, so each half needs its own test <Cite id="worldgym-2025" />. GVL fixes poor naive VLM value prediction by ordering shuffled frames, scoring more than 300 real tasks <Cite id="gvl-2024" />. Runway and DreamDojo used human graders instead, Runway collecting over 16,000 ratings <Cite id="runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026" /> <Cite id="dreamdojo-2026" />.

<span id="level-4-policy-ranking" />
## Level 4: the best simulators order policies as real trials do

A policy evaluator must reproduce reality's ordering, measured as Pearson correlation and Mean Maximum Rank Violation (MMRV) <Cite id="runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026" />. Real comparisons often rest on 10 to 50 trials, and adding trials after peeking risks p-hacking; the STEP sequential test cuts trials by up to 32% <Cite id="optimal-stopping-2025" />.

<Image id="roboarena-evaluation-2025" />

Google DeepMind reports its Veo simulator ranked eight Gemini Robotics checkpoints against more than 1,600 real evaluations at MMRV 0.03, though its absolute success predictions ran low <Cite id="veo-world-simulator-2025" />. WorldGym reached r = 0.78 <Cite id="worldgym-2025" />, and NVIDIA reports r = 0.995 for DreamDojo <Cite id="dreamdojo-2026" />. Runway reports Pearson 0.95 and MMRV 0.033 over eight RoboArena policies, testing ranking only <Cite id="runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026" />. PolaRiS found that Ctrl-World "produces heavy hallucinations during object interaction", mis-ranking policies at MMRV 0.22 <Cite id="polaris-2025" />.

Physics simulation sets the bar. In June 2026, Yuke Zhu and colleagues reported that SimFoundry, which rebuilds a real scene in simulation from video, predicted real results across 7 tasks and 5 policy architectures at mean Pearson 0.911 and MMRV 0.018 <Cite id="simfoundry-2026" />. PolaRiS reports r = 0.9 against real trials <Cite id="polaris-2025" />, and X2Real 0.84 <Cite id="x2real-2026" />.

<span id="level-5-closed-loop-usefulness" />
## Level 5: planning and fine-tuning in a world model improved outcomes

IRASim planning raised Push-T IoU from 0.637 to 0.961 <Cite id="irasim-2024" />, and fine-tuning on Ctrl-World's imagined successes raised policy success by 44.7% <Cite id="ctrl-world-2025" />. Post-training on action-observation data helped more than a stronger pretrained video generator <Cite id="world-in-world-2025" />.

SIMPLER's test, whether simulated and real policy performance correlate under matched visual and physical conditions, applies to learned simulators too <Cite id="simpler-2024" />. RoboArena widens real evaluation beyond one laboratory <Cite id="roboarena-2025" />.

<span id="control-the-evaluation-shifts" />
## Saturated benchmarks hide robustness gaps

Use a factorial matrix to expose shifts one "unseen" split could conceal. RoboLab-120 sorts 120 tasks into visual, procedural and relational axes and measures sensitivity to controlled perturbations <Cite id="robolab-2026" />:

<EvalShiftTable className="my-6" />

LIBERO-Plus used such perturbations to uncover gaps a saturated benchmark hid <Cite id="libero-plus-2025" />, and PolaRiS found nearly all tested policies scoring 90 to 95% on LIBERO, poorly correlated with real performance <Cite id="polaris-2025" />.

<span id="leakage-and-circularity" />
## Disjoint data and blind trials guard against leakage

Foundation models can see the benchmark in pretraining video, and scorers can share a backbone with the policy. Ctrl-World trains on DROID <Cite id="ctrl-world-2025" />, which spans 564 scenes <Cite id="droid-2024" />, and Runway's RoboArena ranking put pi05_droid first <Cite id="runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026" />. X2Real enforces "strictly disjoint training-evaluation pipelines" <Cite id="x2real-2026" />, and TRI compared policies in blind, randomized trials <Cite id="tri-lbm-2025" />.

<span id="the-minimum-credible-report" />
## A credible report pins the benchmark version and the real anchor

A credible report states the use case, action representation, horizon and real anchor, and separates generator from scorer error. It names the benchmark version: Physics-IQ Verified refined 57.6% of samples and shifted rankings at Kendall's τ = 0.46 <Cite id="physics-iq-verified-2026" />. By 1X's arithmetic, with a 15% real gap between two policies, a 70%-accurate world model picks the better one 90% of the time <Cite id="1x-world-model-2025" />.

## Level 4: the best simulators order policies as real trials do

A policy evaluator must reproduce reality's ordering, measured as Pearson correlation and Mean Maximum Rank Violation (MMRV) <Cite id="runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026" />. Real comparisons often rest on 10 to 50 trials, and adding trials after peeking risks p-hacking; the STEP sequential test cuts trials by up to 32% <Cite id="optimal-stopping-2025" />.

<Image id="roboarena-evaluation-2025" />

Use a factorial matrix to expose shifts one "unseen" split could conceal. RoboLab-120 sorts 120 tasks into visual, procedural and relational axes and measures sensitivity to controlled perturbations <Cite id="robolab-2026" />:

<EvalShiftTable className="my-6" />

LIBERO-Plus used such perturbations to uncover gaps a saturated benchmark hid <Cite id="libero-plus-2025" />, and PolaRiS found nearly all tested policies scoring 90 to 95% on LIBERO, poorly correlated with real performance <Cite id="polaris-2025" />.

UniSim trained policies purely inside such a simulator and deployed them zero-shot in the real world . Switch "Video model" from "Listens to the action" to "Ignores the action", and the two futures from one start frame collapse onto the same picture. The action-sensitivity score falls to near zero while the visual-realism score stays put. Video generators show this split: "visual realism does not imply physical understanding" .
## Cosmos 3 replaces a stack of separate models with one omni-model NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 report calls a home robot built from a separate VLM planner, VLA or WAM, and forward-dynamics model "fragmented" and "computationally wasteful" . Cosmos 3, launched at GTC Taipei on 31 May 2026, unifies those capabilities in one omni-model . Its predecessor Predict2.5 had already combined text-, image- and video-conditioned generation in one flow-based model . Its Mixture-of-Transformers backbone routes language and ViT-encoded vision to a causal autoregressive reasoner and VAE-encoded vision, audio and actions to a diffusion generator; diffusion tokens attend to both streams, while reasoner tokens never read diffusion tokens . It supports VLM understanding, video generation and three action modes: forward dynamics (video from clean actions), inverse dynamics (actions from clean video) and policy (both). Specialized results come from separate post-training, such as a DROID policy started from mid-trained Cosmos3-Nano with fresh action modules. Nano has 16B parameters on a dense 8B transformer and Super 64B on a dense 32B one . ## Genie 3 renders worlds at 24 fps that hold for a few minutes The original Genie learned latent actions and generated 2D worlds at about one frame per second . Genie 2 (December 2024) moved to 3D, with consistent worlds for up to a minute and most examples lasting 10 to 20 seconds . In its August 5, 2025 announcement, DeepMind describes Genie 3 as a limited research preview: text-prompted worlds navigable in real time at 24 fps and 720p, largely consistent for a few minutes. A SIMA agent sent navigation actions to Genie 3, and the world model simulated the future without knowing the agent's goal; the test involved no robot manipulation. It lists five limits: a constrained direct action space, multi-agent interaction, geographic accuracy, legible text only when supplied, and a few minutes of continuous interaction . Project Genie, released in January 2026 for AI Ultra subscribers, caps sessions at 60 seconds per world . ## GR-1 and GR-2 built on video pre-training; GR-3 switched to a VLA GR-1 applied large-scale video generative pre-training to multi-task manipulation, predicting future images and actions end to end. On CALVIN it moved success from 88.9% to 94.9%, and in zero-shot unseen scenes from 53.3% to 85.4% . GR-2 pre-trained on 38 million internet clips and over 50 billion tokens, reporting 97.7% average success across more than 100 tasks . GR-3 then switched to a 4B-parameter VLA . ## World-action models now run as closed-loop robot policies A world-action model (WAM) predicts future video and actions together. NVIDIA reports that DreamZero runs a 14B autoregressive video-diffusion model as a 7 Hz closed-loop policy and more than doubles the generalization of state-of-the-art [VLAs](/manipulation/vla-models/) on real robots . Cosmos Policy post-trains Cosmos-Predict2 with no architectural modifications and reaches 98.5% on LIBERO and 67.1% on RoboCasa . LingBot-VA learns frame prediction and policy execution together, feeding real observations back into its rollouts and overlapping prediction with motor execution . Under perturbation, Cosmos-Policy reached 82.2% on LIBERO-Plus and LingBot-VA 74.2% on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus, while VLAs such as π0.5 matched them on some tasks only with extensive, diverse training . Fast-WAM stays competitive without test-time video generation, while removing video co-training costs far more . OpenWAM (October 2026), from Heng Yu, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Ehsan Adeli and colleagues at Stanford, pretrains the Wan2.2-5B video model causally on more than 10,000 hours of robot video. That training raised video-then-action success on LIBERO-Long from 68.4% to 97.8% over the original Wan2.2-5B. Its action expert can generate jointly, video first, action first or decoupled . Long-WAM (October 2026), from Wei Huang, Linxi Fan, Song Han, Yukang Chen and colleagues at NVIDIA, MIT and HKU, found that longer visual history pays off when the video model was pretrained autoregressively. On RoboCasa GR-1, extending context from 0 to 19.2 seconds raised success from 63.3% to 78.7%, while a bidirectionally pretrained start showed no net gain. On real robots it stacked moving cups in 95% of trials, a task where π0.5 and Fast-WAM succeeded in none of 20 . DreamCan (October 2026), from Chongkai Gao, Jiajun Wu, Li Fei-Fei and colleagues at Stanford, NUS, Harvard and Northwestern, plans with a few generated subgoal images instead of dense video. Its training subgoals are chosen to balance whether a low-level policy can reach each one against how far each moves the task. Over 30 runs per task it scored 0% on drawing a smiley and pouring cereal. The backbone takes 11 seconds per 5 seconds of video, plus 1 second for the IDM . In June 2026, 1X launched a World Model Lab led by Sam Sinha, previously a founding research scientist at Luma AI . Odyssey-2 (October 2025) generates each frame causally from prior frames and user input, streaming a new frame every 50 ms (about 20 fps), steerable by text . ## Weak action conditioning is the field's main bottleneck The 2026 survey lists causal conditioning gaps first among its open challenges and calls weak action conditioning the technical bottleneck. Models trained mostly from observation history and task intent produce futures "semantically plausible or intention-consistent, but not necessarily faithful to the physical consequences of the candidate action" . In closed-loop tests, controllability mattered more than visual quality, and post-training on action-observation data beat upgrading the base generator .
